correctness.rationale: Pairwise independence and fairness force E K=n/2 and Var K=n/4. If K=r+qJ with J integer in {0,...,N}, then (J-a)(J-a-1)>=0 gives the sharp minimum variance delta(1-delta), while J(N-J)>=0 gives the sharp maximum m(N-m). Conversely, the nearest-lattice and endpoint laws have the same mean m and these two endpoint variances, so convex mixing realizes every intermediate variance. Conditional on K=k, choosing a uniform k-subset yields coordinate marginal E K/n=1/2 and pair joint E[K(K-1)]/[n(n-1)]=1/4, proving pairwise independence. Mixing residue-specific constructions realizes every residue law. For n=q^2-1, the half-integer variance obstruction is avoided by parity and grid spacing, while the upper variance bound holds uniformly; at n=q^2-2 the stated residue makes m half-integral and requires variance at least 1/4>n/(4q^2). Fresh exact-rational checks for q=2,...,20 reproduced both the full threshold and the forbidden boundary residue.

value.rationale: The law of a Hamming weight modulo q is a natural global statistic under limited independence. The theorem gives both an exact residue-vertex feasibility criterion and a sharp all-q eventual threshold, together with an explicit exchangeable construction. final_claim: For fair pairwise-independent Bernoulli variables, a residue r modulo q can contain K=sum X_i almost surely exactly when the induced integer variable J=(K-r)/q has mean m=(n-2r)/(2q) in [0,N] and required variance v=n/(4q^2) between delta(1-delta) and m(N-m); consequently every law of K mod q is attainable for every n>=q^2-1, and q^2-1 is the exact eventual threshold.

The theorem is for fair pairwise independence only; biased marginals and k-wise independence for k>=3 impose different moment constraints.
